items.stem: The new bus lane helped to ____ the traffic congestion along Bukit Timah Road.

explain.why: 'aggravate' means to make worse, the opposite of what a bus lane is meant to do.
'elevate' means to raise to a higher position or level, which does not describe reducing congestion.
'evaluate' means to judge the value of something; it does not mean reducing a problem.

solution: The new bus lane helped to alleviate the traffic congestion along Bukit Timah Road.
'alleviate' means to make a problem less severe.

items.stem: The thief managed to ____ the security guards by slipping out through a back window.

explain.why: 'invade' means to enter a place by force to take control, not to escape from people.
'evoke' means to bring a memory or feeling to mind; it cannot take 'the guards' as its object.
'avert' is used with dangers or harm (avert a crisis), not with people.

solution: The thief managed to evade the security guards by slipping out through a back window.
'evade' means to escape from or avoid someone.

items.stem: There was ____ traffic on the PIE during the evening rush hour.

explain.why: 'strong' goes with things like wind or tea; traffic is described as 'heavy'.
'thick' goes with things like fog or soup; traffic is described as 'heavy'.
'big' is not the usual word for traffic; we say 'heavy traffic'.

solution: There was heavy traffic on the PIE during the evening rush hour.
'heavy traffic' is the usual collocation for a lot of vehicles on the road.
items.gloss: heavy traffic = a lot of vehicles

items.stem: The museum has a large ____ of rare coins from different countries.

explain.why: 'crowd' is a large group of people, not of objects.
'bunch' goes with things tied or growing together, such as flowers or keys.
'flock' is used for groups of birds or sheep.

solution: The museum has a large collection of rare coins from different countries.
A group of items gathered by a museum is a 'collection'.
items.gloss: collection = a group of items gathered together

items.stem: After a long period of rest, the footballer made a full ____ from his knee injury.

explain.why: 'rescue' means saving someone from danger, not getting well again.
'repair' is used for fixing objects, not a person's health.
'refund' means money paid back to a customer.

solution: After a long period of rest, the footballer made a full recovery from his knee injury.
'make a full recovery' means to become completely well again.

items.stem: Our class teacher always ____ us to be honest, even when the truth is hard to tell.

explain.why: 'insist' is followed by 'on' or 'that', not by an object plus 'to'.
'suggest' is not followed by an object plus 'to' in this way.
'persist' means to keep doing something and has no object like 'us'.

solution: Our class teacher always urges us to be honest, even when the truth is hard to tell.
'urge someone to do something' means to strongly encourage them to do it.

items.stem: A ____ of bees had built a nest near the school playground.

explain.why: 'herd' is used for cattle, elephants and similar animals.
'flock' is used for birds or sheep.
'pack' is used for wolves or dogs.

solution: A swarm of bees had built a nest near the school playground.
A group of bees is called a 'swarm'.
items.gloss: swarm = a large group of insects

items.stem: She spoke in a ____ voice so as not to wake the baby.

explain.why: 'muffled' describes a sound blocked by something, not a voice kept soft on purpose.
'hoarse' describes a rough, dry voice, often from a sore throat.
'shrill' means high-pitched and piercing, which would wake the baby.

solution: She spoke in a hushed voice so as not to wake the baby.
'hushed' means quiet and soft.

items.stem: The tsunami ____ the coastal village, leaving almost no building standing.

explain.why: 'dampened' means made slightly wet, far too weak for such destruction.
'disturbed' means interrupted or upset, which is too mild for destroying a village.
'dented' means made a small hollow in a surface, which is far too small a harm.

solution: The tsunami devastated the coastal village, leaving almost no building standing.
'devastated' means destroyed on a very large scale.

items.stem: Please ____ the antique vase gently, as it is very fragile.

explain.why: 'seize' means to grab suddenly and forcefully, the opposite of gentle.
'wield' is used for tools or weapons that are swung or used with power.
'hurl' means to throw with great force, which would break a fragile vase.

solution: Please handle the antique vase gently, as it is very fragile.
'handle' means to hold or touch something with the hands.
items.gloss: handle = hold or touch with care

items.stem: The pupils listened ____ as the guest speaker described life in the Antarctic.

explain.why: 'lazily' means without effort, so it does not show careful listening.
'noisily' means making a lot of sound, which does not fit listening to a speaker.
'absently' means without paying attention, the opposite of listening carefully.

solution: The pupils listened attentively as the guest speaker described life in the Antarctic.
'attentively' means with careful attention.

items.stem: The librarian ____ us to return our books before the school holidays.

explain.why: 'remember' cannot be followed by an object plus 'to' to mean telling someone.
'recall' means to bring a memory to mind and is not followed by 'us to'.
'recorded' means wrote down or saved, which does not fit 'us to return'.

solution: The librarian reminded us to return our books before the school holidays.
'remind someone to do something' means to help them remember it.

items.stem: The athlete's ____ determination helped her to finish the marathon despite her leg cramps.

explain.why: 'sporadic' means happening only now and then, which does not fit determination that lasted to the end.
'reluctant' means unwilling and is not used with the noun 'determination'.
'meagre' means very small in amount and is used for things like meals or pay.

solution: The athlete's unwavering determination helped her to finish the marathon despite her leg cramps.
'unwavering' means steady and not changing.

items.stem: Mei Lin is ____ about her work; she checks every answer three times before handing in her paper.

explain.why: 'impulsive' means acting without thinking, the opposite of checking three times.
'indifferent' means not caring, which does not fit someone who checks so carefully.
'spontaneous' means done naturally without planning, which does not fit checking answers repeatedly.

solution: Mei Lin is meticulous about her work; she checks every answer three times before handing in her paper.
'meticulous' means very careful about details.

items.stem: The detective was ____ by the strange footprints that seemed to lead nowhere.

explain.why: 'amused' means finding something funny, which does not fit an unsolved mystery.
'relieved' means free from worry, but footprints leading nowhere would not do that.
'contented' means happy and satisfied, which does not fit the mystery.

solution: The detective was puzzled by the strange footprints that seemed to lead nowhere.
'puzzled' means confused because something cannot be explained.

items.stem: The twins look so alike that even their teachers find it hard to ____ between them.

explain.why: 'disguise' means to change how someone looks so they are not recognised.
'dispose' means to throw away or get rid of something.
'distract' means to draw attention away from something.

solution: The twins look so alike that even their teachers find it hard to distinguish between them.
'distinguish between' means to tell two things apart.

items.stem: The tiny hawker stall managed to ____ despite competition from the new food court.

explain.why: 'revive' means to bring back to life or strength, but the stall never closed.
'derive' means to obtain from a source.
'deprive' means to take something away from someone.

solution: The tiny hawker stall managed to survive despite competition from the new food court.
'survive' means to continue to exist in a difficult situation.

items.stem: His excuse for being late was so ____ that nobody believed him.

explain.why: 'far-reaching' means having wide effects, and it is used for changes or decisions.
'far-sighted' means planning wisely for the future; it describes people, not excuses.
'far-flung' means very distant and describes places.

solution: His excuse for being late was so far-fetched that nobody believed him.
'far-fetched' means very unlikely to be true.

items.stem: The witness's account was full of ____: she first said it was 8 p.m., then 9 p.m.

explain.why: 'assurances' are promises that something is true.
'reminders' are things that help someone remember.
'replacements' are things that take the place of others.

solution: The witness's account was full of inconsistencies: she first said it was 8 p.m., then 9 p.m.
'inconsistencies' are parts that do not agree with each other.
items.gloss: inconsistency = a part that does not agree with another

items.stem: The principal asked the pupils to show more ____ for the cleaners who worked quietly every day.

explain.why: 'apprehension' means worry about something that may happen.
'appearance' means how someone or something looks.
'appointment' means an arranged meeting or a job position.

solution: The principal asked the pupils to show more appreciation for the cleaners who worked quietly every day.
'appreciation' means thankful recognition of someone's effort.

items.stem: The little girl clung ____ to her mother's hand in the crowded MRT station.

explain.why: 'densely' describes things packed closely together, such as a crowd or forest.
'sharply' goes with sudden changes or pointed things, not with clinging.
'tensely' describes how someone waits or feels; it is not used with 'clung'.

solution: The little girl clung tightly to her mother's hand in the crowded MRT station.
'clung tightly' means held on very firmly.

items.stem: The committee will ____ all the pupils' suggestions before making a final decision.

explain.why: 'consult' means to ask a person for advice, so it cannot take 'suggestions' as its object.
'console' means to comfort someone who is sad.
'consume' means to eat, drink or use up.

solution: The committee will consider all the pupils' suggestions before making a final decision.
'consider' means to think about something carefully.

items.stem: The shop assistant politely ____ my request for a refund because I had no receipt.

explain.why: 'deflected' means turned aside, as with a ball or a question.
'deducted' means subtracted an amount from a total.
'declared' means announced something openly.

solution: The shop assistant politely declined my request for a refund because I had no receipt.
'declined' means refused politely.

items.stem: Zack's quick thinking ____ the situation and prevented a fight from breaking out.

explain.why: 'diffused' means spread out, as with light or heat; the word for calming a tense situation is 'defused'.
'refused' means said no to something.
'accused' means said someone had done something wrong.

solution: Zack's quick thinking defused the situation and prevented a fight from breaking out.
'defused' means made a tense situation less dangerous.

items.stem: The company's profits have ____ since the new manager took over; they are now three times higher.

explain.why: 'hovered' means stayed at about the same level, but the profits tripled.
'dwindled' means became smaller, the opposite of tripling.
'plunged' means dropped sharply, the opposite of rising.

solution: The company's profits have soared since the new manager took over; they are now three times higher.
'soared' means rose very quickly to a high level.
items.gloss: soar = rise very high and fast

items.stem: To save electricity, the school ____ the use of air-conditioners to the afternoon.

explain.why: 'retreated' means moved back or withdrew.
'resisted' means fought against something.
'restored' means brought back to its original state.

solution: To save electricity, the school restricted the use of air-conditioners to the afternoon.
'restricted' means limited.

items.stem: The teacher praised Hui Ying for her ____ answer, which covered every point in the question.

explain.why: 'compulsory' means required by rule.
'comparable' means similar enough to be compared.
'competitive' means eager to win.

solution: The teacher praised Hui Ying for her comprehensive answer, which covered every point in the question.
'comprehensive' means complete and covering everything.

items.stem: The beach was ____ after the Sunday crowd had left, with only a few seagulls pecking at scraps.

explain.why: 'deprived' means lacking basic needs.
'desperate' means in great need or without hope.
'defeated' means beaten in a contest.

solution: The beach was deserted after the Sunday crowd had left, with only a few seagulls pecking at scraps.
'deserted' means empty because everyone has left.

items.stem: The thick haze ____ the view of the harbour so that the ships could barely be seen.

explain.why: 'observed' means watched carefully.
'obtained' means got or acquired.
'obliged' means forced someone to do something.

solution: The thick haze obscured the view of the harbour so that the ships could barely be seen.
'obscured' means made hard to see.

items.stem: My aunt's bakery is ____, with long queues outside every morning.

explain.why: 'drifting' means moving slowly without direction.
'lingering' means staying longer than needed.
'shrinking' means becoming smaller, which does not fit long queues of customers.

solution: My aunt's bakery is thriving, with long queues outside every morning.
'thriving' means growing and doing very well.

items.stem: We must ____ water during the dry spell so that the reservoirs do not run low.

explain.why: 'conceal' means to hide something from view.
'concede' means to admit that something is true or to give in.
'convert' means to change something into another form.

solution: We must conserve water during the dry spell so that the reservoirs do not run low.
'conserve' means to use carefully and avoid waste.

items.stem: The old man's ____ remarks made the children giggle.

explain.why: 'weary' means very tired.
'wary' means careful about possible danger.
'wasteful' means using more than is needed.

solution: The old man's witty remarks made the children giggle.
'witty' means clever and amusing in speech.

items.stem: Before the experiment, Mr Lee gave the pupils ____ instructions so that no one would be hurt.

explain.why: 'explosive' describes something that can blow up, not instructions.
'expensive' means costing a lot of money.
'excessive' means more than is needed, which does not say the instructions were clear.

solution: Before the experiment, Mr Lee gave the pupils explicit instructions so that no one would be hurt.
'explicit' means clearly and fully stated.

items.stem: The villagers were ____ to leave their homes even though the flood waters were rising.

explain.why: 'resistant' is followed by 'to' plus a noun, as in 'resistant to change', not by an infinitive.
'reliable' means able to be trusted.
'relevant' means connected to the matter being discussed.

solution: The villagers were reluctant to leave their homes even though the flood waters were rising.
'reluctant to do something' means unwilling to do it.

items.stem: The runner ____ across the finish line, completely out of breath.

explain.why: 'strolled' means walked in a slow, relaxed way, which does not fit someone out of breath.
'strutted' means walked proudly with the chest out.
'skipped' means moved with light hops, which does not fit a tired runner.

solution: The runner staggered across the finish line, completely out of breath.
'staggered' means walked unsteadily from tiredness.
